Subject: MSA fee ladder consolidation + implementation notes

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, attached are the MSA redlines and a draft Exhibit F that consolidates the previous fee ladder into a single tiered schedule and adds a short amortization clause for one-time implementation credits. The main asks from MediWell we captured were:

- Consolidate hourly/seat-based surcharges into a single throughput tier (see Section 3.1 in redline).
- Preserve current SLA commitments (latency percentiles) — we will not change SLO language.
- Add an explicit top-up/change-order flow for burst capacity (Exhibit F, Appendix A).
- Amortize the onboarding credit across first 12 months (finance asked for this).

Action items:
1) Please confirm procurement will accept fee-ladder consolidation in principle (does it need internal approval from your billing team?).
2) Confirm whether MediWell requires an invoice milestone split (we proposed single invoice at contract effective date + monthly usage).
3) If you want alternative wording for amortization timing, note it here and we can update before legal review.

Attachments: MSA_redline_v3.pdf (redline), SOW_Exhibit-F_draft.docx (exhibit with top-up flow).

If this looks good, we’ll route to Legal (Karthik) and Finance (Laura) for sign-off and then send for signature via DocuSign.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Irene — appreciate the summary and the redlines. A few quick questions from procurement and billing side:

1) Billing triggers: If we accept the consolidated fee ladder, will the committed throughput be billed in arrears or upfront? We normally prefer monthly in arrears for committed usage.
2) Credits: The amortization approach is fine, but procurement asks that credits be explicitly capped (we cannot have open-ended credit application against future surges). Can you confirm a 12-month cap?
3) SLA + penalties: You mentioned SLA unchanged; do you have the SLO/credit table we can include as an appendix so our legal can see the penalty thresholds?

I’ve attached our standard procurement form (Procurement_Form_MediWell.pdf) — it notes preferred invoicing cadence and our internal PO process.

Once we have these clarified, I’ll route to our billing lead for a final thumbs-up.

Best,
Priya Sharma
Head of Procurement — MediWell Health

Hi all — looping in the redline suggestions from Legal. I reviewed MSA_redline_v3 and propose the following edits before we send a final to MediWell legal:

- Section 2.4 (Billing): Add explicit language that committed throughput will be invoiced monthly in arrears unless otherwise agreed in writing (this should address Priya’s preference).
- Section 3.1 (Fee Ladder): Retain consolidated tiers but add a short note that pricing tiers are fixed for the initial 12-month term and subject to renegotiation at renewal.
- Exhibit F (Top-up / Change Order): Add a bullet that top-up costs will be calculated at the consolidated tier rate and may be invoiced within the next billing cycle; include example calculation.
- Credit amortization: Accept 12-month cap per procurement but require a recovery clause if contract is terminated early (pro-rate remaining credit).

I attached a small redline (MSA_redline_v3_KI_comments.pdf) with the exact text suggestions and a draft SLO appendix (SLO_Table_v1.xlsx) we can append for clarity on penalty thresholds.

If MediWell accepts monthly-in-arrears invoicing and the 12-month credit cap with the early termination pro-rate, Legal is comfortable routing to Finance for final sign-off. Laura — can you confirm finance okay with the amortization + pro-rate?

Thanks,
Karthik
Counsel, Redwood Inference
